transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… it’s kind of embarrassing, but I’m here because of wasps. I mean, I used to love being outside in the summer—my garden, the church flower beds, all that—and now I plan practically everything around not running into them. 

If I hear buzzing by the back porch, I won’t go out there, and I make my husband unload things instead. I even stopped helping with the garden jobs at church, which bothers me because I liked doing that, and you know, the ladies there depend on people showing up. It’s just gotten to where summer feels like something I have to get through instead of enjoy.
Is your fear mainly just about wasps?

Yes, mostly wasps. I mean, bees too if I’m not looking close, but it’s really the wasps that set me off. And I know that sounds silly because they’re just little insects—my neighbor will just wave one away and keep talking like nothing happened. But for me, if one gets near me, it feels like something awful is about to happen. My whole mind just goes right there, like I need to get away.
When a wasp gets near you, do you suddenly get physical panic symptoms like your heart racing or trouble breathing?

Yes—right away. Like, the second I hear that sharp buzzing by the porch, or I see one kind of hovering around the flowers, my heart just jumps. My hands start shaking, and I feel like I have to get inside immediately.

It’s funny, because my husband can stand there with the grocery bags and act like it’s nothing, and I’m already halfway to the door before I even think about it.
Did this fear start after you were stung by a wasp?

I’m not really sure. I can’t point to one big sting and say, “That’s when it started.” I mean, I’ve been around them forever—yard work, picnics, church flowers—and you hear stories, you know, somebody’s cousin getting stung at a barbecue and swelling up, that sort of thing. But for me, I don’t remember one specific wasp sting that explains it. It just kind of… got worse over time, I guess.
Outside of wasps, do you find yourself worrying a lot about many other everyday things?

I don’t think so… I mean, I worry about normal things, like the house or whether I remembered to pay a bill, and then my daughter will call and I’ll get distracted talking about her kids’ school stuff. But I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying about everything all day.

It’s more that the wasp thing just takes over when it happens. Other everyday things don’t hit me like that, not really.
Do you feel your fear of wasps is stronger than the actual danger they usually pose?

Yes, I suppose it is. I mean, I know in my head it’s just a little insect, and other people just wave it away or keep eating their sandwich like nothing’s happening.

But when one comes near me, it doesn’t feel little. It feels like something awful is about to happen, like I need to get away right that second. My sister-in-law, she’ll sit outside with iced tea and not even flinch, and I’m over there watching every flowerpot like it’s going to attack me. So yes… I know it’s probably stronger than the actual danger.
